title: Tick Tock Counter
statement: Count from 1 to N. For multiples of 3 print Tick, for multiples of 5 print Tock, for multiples of both print TickTock, otherwise print the number.
hint: Check divisibility by 15 (or build the string from both checks) before checking 3 or 5 alone.

samples.out:
1
2
Tick
4
Tock
Tick
7
8
Tick
Tock
11
Tick
13
14
TickTock

title: Busiest Shop
statement: There are R shops and each shop recorded sales on C days. A shop's total is the sum of its row. Print the largest total.
input: First line R C. Next R lines each have C integers.
hint: Sum each row in an inner loop and keep the best total seen so far.

title: Halve or Decrement
statement: Start with N. In one move, if the number is even divide it by 2, otherwise subtract 1. Print how many moves it takes to reach 0.
hint: Just simulate with a while loop. Use long in Java.

title: Digits That Divide
statement: Given a positive integer N, count how many of its digits divide N exactly. Count repeated digits each time they appear, and skip zeros.
hint: Peel digits with % 10 on a copy of N, and test N % digit == 0 on the original.

title: Mirror Number
statement: Print YES if the integer N reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise NO. Negative numbers are never mirrors.
hint: Reverse the number with rev = rev * 10 + n % 10 and compare it with the original. Try it without converting to a string.

title: Add One to a Digit Array
statement: A large number is given as its N digits, most significant first. Add 1 to it and print the digits of the result separated by spaces.
input: First line N. Second line N digits (no leading zero unless the number is 0).
output: Digits of the result, space separated.
hint: Walk from the last digit. A 9 becomes 0 and carries; any other digit just goes up by one and you stop. If every digit was 9, put a 1 in front.

title: Reverse a Number
statement: Given a non-negative integer N, print it with its digits reversed. Leading zeros in the result are dropped (so 1200 becomes 21).
hint: Build the answer as rev = rev * 10 + N % 10 while N > 0.

title: Sum of Digits
statement: Given a non-negative integer N, print the sum of its digits.
output: One integer: the sum of the digits of N.
hint: Repeatedly take N % 10 to get the last digit, then do N / 10. Use long in Java.

title: Prime or Not
statement: For each of T numbers, print YES if it is prime, otherwise NO.
input: First line T. Next T lines each contain one integer N.
hint: You only need to try divisors up to √N. Remember 1 is not prime.

title: GCD and LCM
statement: Given two positive integers A and B, print their greatest common divisor and least common multiple.
output: Two integers: GCD and LCM, separated by a space.
hint: Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b). Then lcm = a / gcd * b, which needs long in Java.

title: Running Sum
statement: Given an array of N integers, print the running (prefix) sum: the i-th output is a[0] + a[1] + … + a[i].
hint: Keep one running total and add each element to it. The total can exceed int, so use long in Java.

title: Even-Length Numbers
statement: Given N positive integers, count how many have an even number of digits.
hint: Count digits by dividing by 10 until the number is 0, then check the count is even.

title: Strip a Value
statement:
Remove every occurrence of V from the array, keeping the other elements in their original order. Print how many remain, then the remaining elements.

Try doing it in place with one write pointer.
input: First line N V. Second line N integers.
output: First line the new length K. Second line the K remaining elements (empty if K = 0).
hint: Keep w = 0. For each element not equal to V, copy it to a[w] and increase w.

title: Dedupe a Sorted Array
statement: The array is sorted in non-decreasing order. Keep only the first copy of each value. Print how many distinct values there are, then those values in order.
input: First line N. Second line N sorted integers.
output: First line K. Second line the K distinct values.
hint: Because equal values sit together, compare each element with the last one you kept.

title: Was It Sorted, Then Rotated?
statement: Print YES if the array could be a non-decreasing array that was rotated some number of positions (including zero), otherwise NO.
hint: Count places where a[i] > a[(i+1) % N], wrapping around. A rotated sorted array has at most one such drop.

title: Squares, Still Sorted
statement:
The array is sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain negatives. Print the squares of all elements, sorted in non-decreasing order.

Can you do it in O(N) without sorting again?
input: First line N. Second line N sorted integers.
hint: The largest square is at one of the two ends. Use two pointers and fill the answer from the back.

title: Best Single Trade
statement: p[i] is the price of a stock on day i. Buy on one day and sell on a later day. Print the maximum profit, or 0 if no trade makes money.
hint: Track the cheapest price so far. Each day, the best sale today is price minus that minimum.

title: Rotate Array Right
statement:
Rotate an array of N integers to the right by K steps and print it.

Rotating [1 2 3 4 5] right by 2 gives [4 5 1 2 3].
input: First line N K. Second line N integers.
hint: Rotating by N changes nothing, so use K % N. Element i moves to (i + K) % N.

title: Second Largest Element
statement: Given an array of N integers, print the second largest distinct value. If it does not exist, print -1.
output: The second largest distinct value, or -1.
hint: One pass: keep first and second. When you see a bigger value, the old first becomes second. Skip values equal to first.

title: Move Zeros to End
statement: Move all zeros of the array to the end while keeping the order of the non-zero elements, then print the array.
hint: Keep a pointer w for the next write position. Copy each non-zero to a[w++], then fill the rest with zeros.

title: Pair With Target Sum
statement: Is there a pair of different positions i ≠ j with a[i] + a[j] = T? Print YES or NO.
input: First line N T. Second line N integers.
hint: Walk the array once. Before adding x to a set, check whether T − x is already in it.

title: Any Repeats?
statement: Print YES if some value appears at least twice in the array, otherwise NO.
hint: Add values to a HashSet as you go; if one is already there, you found a repeat.

title: Same Letters?
statement: Two lowercase words are given. Print YES if one is a rearrangement of the other (same letters, same counts), otherwise NO.
hint: Use an int[26] array: add counts for the first word, subtract for the second, and check everything is zero.

title: Cut-Out Letters
statement: You want to spell a note by cutting letters out of a magazine. Each magazine letter can be used once. Print YES if it's possible, otherwise NO.
input: First line the note. Second line the magazine. Both lowercase.
hint: Count the magazine's letters, then spend one count for each letter of the note. If a count goes below zero, it's impossible.

title: First Unique Character
statement: Given a lowercase string S, print the index (0-based) of the first character that appears exactly once. If none exists, print -1.
hint: First pass: count every letter in an array of 26. Second pass: return the first index whose count is 1.

title: Common Values
statement: Print every distinct value that appears in both arrays, in increasing order. If there are none, print -1.
input: Line 1 N, line 2 the first array. Line 3 M, line 4 the second array.
output: The common values in increasing order, or -1.
hint: Put the first array in a set, then collect values of the second that are in it (into another set to avoid duplicates), and sort.

title: Letter Families
statement: Group the words so that words made of exactly the same letters are together. Inside each group sort the words alphabetically (keep duplicates). Print one group per line, and order the lines by comparing the groups word by word (alphabetically, like sorting lists).
input: First line N. Second line N lowercase words.
output: One line per group, words separated by spaces.
hint: The sorted letters of a word are its key, e.g. eat → aet. Map key → list of words, then sort each list and the list of groups.

samples.in:
6
eat tea tan ate nat bat
samples.out:
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan

title: Longest Run of Consecutive Values
statement: Values in the array are unsorted. Find the length of the longest set of values x, x+1, x+2, … that are all present. Aim for O(N).
output: The length of the longest run.
hint: Put everything in a set. Only start counting from x when x − 1 is not in the set, so each run is walked once.

title: Most Frequent Element
statement: Print the value that appears most often in the array. If several values tie, print the smallest of them.
hint: Count with a HashMap / dict, then scan the counts for the best (value, count) pair.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Two arrays are already sorted. Merge them into one sorted array in a single pass, without calling a sort function.
input: Line 1: N. Line 2: N sorted integers. Line 3: M. Line 4: M sorted integers.
hint: Two pointers i and j: always take the smaller of x[i] and y[j], then copy whatever is left.

title: Out of Line
statement: Students should stand in non-decreasing order of height. Given the current line, print how many positions hold the wrong height compared with the sorted line.
hint: Make a sorted copy and compare position by position. With heights ≤ 100, counting sort works too.

title: Sort by a Given Order
statement: Array B has distinct values and defines an order. Rearrange array A so values that appear in B come first, in B's order. Values not in B go at the end in increasing order.
input: Line 1 N, line 2 array A. Line 3 M, line 4 array B.
hint: Map each value of B to its index, then sort A with a comparator: known values by index, unknown values after them by value.

title: Biggest Triangle
statement: Pick three of the given stick lengths to form a triangle with positive area (each side shorter than the other two combined). Print the largest possible perimeter, or 0 if no triangle is possible.
hint: Sort descending. For the longest side a[i], the best partners are the next two; check a[i] < a[i+1] + a[i+2].

title: Sort the Array
statement: Print the array in non-decreasing order. Try writing a simple sort yourself first (bubble, selection or insertion), then compare with the built-in sort.
hint: Insertion sort: take each element and shift bigger elements one step right until you find its place.

title: Author Score
statement: An author's papers have the given citation counts. Their score is the largest h such that at least h papers have h or more citations each. Print h.
input: First line N. Second line N citation counts.
hint: Sort in descending order. The paper at index i (0-based) supports h = i + 1 if it has at least i + 1 citations.

title: K-th Smallest
statement: Print the K-th smallest element of the array (counting duplicates, 1-based).
input: First line N K. Second line N integers.
hint: Sort, then the answer sits at index K − 1.

title: Diagonal Sum
statement: Given an N × N matrix, print the sum of both diagonals. If N is odd, count the centre cell only once.
input: First line N N. Next N lines, each with N integers.
hint: Main diagonal is [i][i], the other is [i][N−1−i]. Subtract the centre once when N is odd.

title: Transpose a Matrix
statement: Print the transpose of an R × C matrix: row i of the answer is column i of the input.
input: First line R C. Next R lines, each with C integers.
hint: Answer cell [j][i] = input cell [i][j]. Loop j on the outside when printing.

title: Refold a Grid
statement: Read the R × C grid row by row and refill a new NR × NC grid in the same row-by-row order. If the sizes don't hold the same number of cells, print the original grid unchanged.
input: First line R C, then R rows. Last line NR NC.
output: The resulting grid, one row per line.
hint: Cell number k in reading order lives at (k / C, k % C) in the old grid and goes to (k / NC, k % NC) in the new one.

title: Turn a Square Grid Clockwise
statement: Rotate the N × N grid 90° clockwise and print it. Try doing it in place.
hint: Clockwise rotation = transpose (swap m[i][j] and m[j][i]), then reverse each row.

title: Spiral Order
statement: Print all cells of an R × C matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting from the top-left.
input: First line R C. Next R lines, each with C integers.
hint: Keep four walls: top, bottom, left, right. Walk one edge, then move that wall inward. Check the walls haven't crossed before the bottom and left edges.

title: Zero Spread
statement: For every cell that is 0 in the original grid, set its whole row and whole column to 0. Print the result.
hint: First record which rows and which columns contain a zero, then do a second pass to write zeros. Don't zero while you're still scanning.

title: Is This Sudoku Legal?
statement: A partly filled 9 × 9 Sudoku grid uses digits 1–9 and . for empty cells. Print YES if no row, column or 3 × 3 box contains the same digit twice, otherwise NO. You don't need to check whether it can be solved.
input: 9 lines, each with 9 tokens separated by spaces.
hint: Use 27 sets (or boolean arrays): one per row, column and box. Box index is (r / 3) * 3 + c / 3.

title: Find in a Sorted Grid
statement: Each row of the grid is sorted left to right, and the first value of each row is larger than the last value of the row above. Answer Q queries: is value x in the grid? Aim for O(log(R·C)) per query.
input: First line R C, then R rows. Next line Q, then a line of Q query values.
hint: Read the grid as one sorted array of length R·C. Index k is cell (k / C, k % C), so plain binary search works.

title: Two Values, One Target
statement: The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. Return the 1-based positions [i, j] (i < j) of the two values that add up to target. Exactly one answer exists.
hint: Start one pointer at each end. If the sum is too small move the left pointer right, if too big move the right pointer left.

title: Reverse In Place
statement: Reverse the array of characters s in place. Your function returns nothing; we check s afterwards.
hint: Swap s[i] and s[n-1-i] while i is in the first half.

title: Stack That Knows Its Minimum
statement:
Design a stack supporting push, pop, top and getMin, all in O(1).

Input line 1 is the list of operations, line 2 their arguments. The output lists each call's return value (null for calls that return nothing).
constraints: At most 3·10<sup>4</sup> calls; pop/top/getMin only on a non-empty stack.
hint: Store (value, min so far) pairs.

title: Flip the Chain
statement: Reverse the singly linked list starting at head and return the new head.
hint: Keep prev, cur, next. Point cur.next to prev and move forward.
